newsitem.title: USA: Salomon Brothers Nov same-store sales index up.
newsitem.headline: Salomon Brothers Nov same-store sales index up.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said Thursday its same-store sales growth index for retailers rose 3.9 percent in November, compared with a 2.9 percent rise a year ago.

"In general, November sales gains were positively impacted by an improving environment for apparel and relatively easy comparisons," Salomon analysts said in a research report. "Concurrently, we believe that lower levels of discounting and strong inventory and expense controls have positioned the major retailers well in terms of profitability."
The November increase also compared with a 4.8 percent gain in the index in October.
Salomon said that, because of a "significant shift" in the calendar, it believes the Christmas selling season should be analyzed on a two-month basis combining November and December.

"For the industry as a whole, as mentioned, apparel sales continued their relatively favorable trend," Salomon said. "In addition, given the rather easy year-to-year comparisons in the fourth quarter of 1996, we expect favorable sales and earnings performances."
The report also stated that the recent underperformance of retail stocks in general versus the overall market provides opportunities in some growth- and value-oriented retailers.
